title: Did the Contract Follow the Company?
scenario_text: Opal Health's legal ops team must determine who its counterparty is under a data-processing MSA after a corporate transaction. The original counterparty, "Trellis Clinical Data, Inc.," signed a three-year MSA with Opal Health for de-identified analytics services, $1.2M annually. The MSA's assignment clause reads: "Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except that either party may assign to a successor in connection with a merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and this Agreement binds permitted successors and assigns." On 2024-04-01, Trellis Clinical Data, Inc. was acquired by "Marrow Analytics Corp." through a statutory merger in which Trellis merged into Marrow, with Marrow as the surviving legal entity; Trellis Clinical Data, Inc. ceased to exist and all its rights and obligations vested in Marrow by operation of law. Marrow now sends invoices and service reports under its own name, referencing the same MSA number, and has continued performing the analytics without interruption. Opal Health's compliance officer asks whether the MSA is still in force and enforceable against Marrow, or whether a new contract must be negotiated before continuing to send protected data. Because the analytics involve protected health data under a business-associate arrangement, Opal Health cannot keep transmitting records to a party it is not under contract with.
question: Is Marrow Analytics Corp. now Opal Health's counterparty under the existing MSA, and is the MSA enforceable against it?
choices: Yes; the MSA transferred to Marrow as the surviving entity and remains in force, because the assignment clause permits assignment to a successor in a merger and binds permitted successors.
No; the MSA did not transfer to Marrow; it remains with the original Trellis entity, so Opal Health must execute a new contract (or a consented assignment) with Marrow before sending protected data.
Yes, but only if Marrow signs a fresh MSA, because a contract can never bind an entity that was not the original signatory under any circumstances.
The MSA automatically terminated on the transaction date regardless of structure, so neither Trellis nor Marrow has any continuing obligation.
